merger_name: Woolworths – supermarket site in Shepparton North, VIC
merger_description:
Woolworths Group Limited’s (**Woolworths**) wholly-owned subsidiary, Fabcot Pty Ltd (**Fabcot**), proposes to acquire a freehold interest in vacant land located at 38 Ford Road, Parts 219, 221–229 & 231–237 Numurkah Road, 10 Ford Road, and 5 Grant Court, in Shepparton, Victoria (together, the **Target Site**) from North Shepparton Commercial Pty Ltd and Ford Rd Enterprises Pty Ltd (the **Acquisition**).

Woolworths is an ASX-listed retailer operating a national supermarket network, including full-line Woolworths Supermarkets, Woolworths Metro outlets and online grocery services, together with other retail and consumer businesses.

Fabcot acquires and develops non-residential property for the Woolworths Group’s retail network. Fabcot intends to develop a shopping centre at the Target Site.

The shopping centre will include a full-line supermarket and ‘Online Hub’ (to be operated by Woolworths), a discount supermarket, specialty retail and pad sites, car spaces and other amenities.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) has considered the
information provided with the notification waiver application and had
regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided, the ACCC is unable to reach a
view that the Acquisition would not be likely to raise competition
issues in any market. It considers that the Acquisition warrants
consideration through the notification process, including via further
information gathering and consultation with third parties. This may
include a focus on:
a. Woolworths’ share of supply of grocery products and gross
lettable area in Shepparton North and the surrounding local
areas
b. the extent that population growth in the local area of
Shepparton North could support a material increase in
supermarket capacity given its regional location
c. the extent to which Woolworths is likely to be constrained by
existing or proposed grocery retailers in the surrounding local
area of Shepparton North.
The ACCC does not consider it necessary to reach a concluded view
on the likelihood of the Acquisition meeting the notification
thresholds. The ACCC observes that based on the information
provided in the application, the Acquisition may meet the notification
thresholds determined under subsection 51ABQ(1) of the Act.
Given the above, the ACCC has determined not to make the
notification waiver determination applied for.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
